AI Sales Assistant Chatbot for Pharmaceutical Consultants

A trusted knowledge workspace that helps field consultants search medical content, analyse documents, reuse previous answers and learn from colleagues across regions.

01 — Understanding the problem

Uncovering how consultants find and share knowledge

Sales consultants needed quick, credible answers during client conversations, but information was spread across documents, previous chats and colleagues' local expertise.

The research reframed the product from a simple question-answer tool into a searchable, reusable and collaborative knowledge environment.

⌕

Search had to accept more than text

Consultants expected to search with text, images, video and uploaded documents, then receive concise answers with linked source material.

↺

Useful answers were being recreated

Previous searches were difficult to retrieve, filter or tag. Favourites, pinning and organised history became core product requirements.

◎

Regional context lived with people

Teams needed a structured way to ask colleagues, discover regional discussions and turn individual expertise into shared organisational knowledge.

“
The opportunity was not another chatbot. It was a trusted workspace where every useful answer could become reusable knowledge.

This principle guided the information architecture, interaction model and visual system.

02 — Structuring the experience

Turning scattered requirements into one connected journey

The solution architecture centred on three connected behaviours: ask a new question, leverage previous knowledge and participate in the wider consultant network.

Outputs were designed to be actionable—read, copy, download, filter, save, pin or share—rather than ending at a single AI response.

1. Start with the taskText, image, camera and document inputs meet consultants where the question begins.
2. Build on historySearch history, favourites and tags reduce repeated work and preserve context.
3. Extend through peopleRegional queries and groups make colleague knowledge discoverable and reusable.
03 — Designing the system

A visual language built for speed, trust and clarity

The interface uses a restrained medical palette, clear type hierarchy and repeatable card patterns. Red marks primary action, while status colours and neutral surfaces keep dense enterprise screens easy to scan.

Trust before novelty

Sources, categories, timestamps and context remain visible around AI output.

Fast recognition

Consistent icons, badges and card anatomy reduce the effort needed to scan results.

Reusable components

One system supports chats, groups, regional queries, analytics and future modules.

From tokens to complete product patterns

The design system defines colour, typography, buttons, cards, badges, form elements and distinct conversation styles for the AI assistant and the consultant.

  • Primary red for actions and active states
  • Deep navy for hierarchy and legibility
  • Neutral surfaces for information-heavy layouts
  • Soft gradients reserved for human messages
04 — Final solution

One workspace for discovery, conversation and collective intelligence

The final product brings AI-assisted search, document analysis, saved knowledge, organised groups and regional conversations into a consistent enterprise experience.

01

Operational visibility

The dashboard makes adoption visible without overwhelming the user, combining key metrics with document and interaction patterns.

  • High-level usage and conversation metrics
  • Document mix and trend reporting
  • Clear route to deeper business intelligence
02

Regional knowledge becomes discoverable

The regional hub surfaces market-specific questions, colleague participation and trending discussions so teams can learn beyond their immediate network.

  • Region-based entry points and query counts
  • Discussion activity and participant context
  • Trending signals for fast prioritisation
03

Organised group knowledge

Chat Groups turn scattered conversations into shared workspaces organised by therapeutic area or project, helping consultants find the right context without searching through every individual chat.

  • Therapeutic-area and project-based organisation
  • Conversation, member and creation-date context
  • Expandable groups that keep nested chats easy to scan
04

Fast access to saved work

Favourite Chats bring high-value conversations back into view through search, category filters and structured cards, so useful answers remain easy to retrieve after the original interaction.

  • Search, category filters and sorting controls
  • Tags, summaries and recency cues for quick scanning
  • Direct access back into important conversations
05

Actions remain within context

Conversation management stays inside the active workspace, allowing consultants to save, organise or remove a chat without interrupting the question-and-answer flow.

  • Save a chat without leaving the conversation
  • Add the discussion to a group or favourites
  • Delete controls remain available from the same menu
05 — Product impact

Impact goes beyond faster search

The concept creates a foundation for governed AI, reusable organisational knowledge and more connected pharmaceutical field teams.

01

Faster answer discovery

Multimodal input, concise summaries and linked material shorten the route from question to usable response.

02

Less duplicated effort

History, favourites, tags and groups turn previous work into a reliable starting point instead of a dead end.

03

Stronger regional learning

Market-specific discussions make local expertise visible while preserving the context behind each answer.

04

Scalable governance

A consistent design system and visible source context support future permissions, review flows and compliance controls.

Prototype success criteria

Measurable product outcomes

These targets frame how the concept should be validated in usability testing and a controlled pilot.

65%

Faster time to a usable answer

Compare completion time against the current document-and-colleague search process.

90%

Task completion for core journeys

Measure new search, saved chat retrieval and regional query participation.

35%

More reuse of existing knowledge

Track how often consultants open, save or share previously created answers.

Targets shown here are validation goals for the concept, not claimed production results.

What the process reinforced

Three principles worth carrying forward

01 / Trust

AI confidence comes from visible context

Source material, categories, timestamps and colleague activity help users judge an answer rather than simply accept it.

02 / Reuse

Search history is a product surface

Saved conversations need structure, filters and meaningful metadata before they can become organisational knowledge.

03 / Network

People remain part of the answer

Regional queries and groups complement AI by preserving market nuance and peer experience.

Next steps

From polished concept to validated product

The next phase should test trust, speed and knowledge reuse with real consultants, then refine the system around compliance and enterprise integration needs.

01

Run scenario-based usability testing

Validate search, document upload, save, group and regional query flows using representative field tasks.

02

Define evidence and review states

Clarify source quality, medical review, expiration and escalation patterns for sensitive information.

03

Connect enterprise systems

Map permissions, identity, content repositories, analytics and approved response workflows.

04

Pilot, measure and iterate

Use the stated success criteria to evaluate whether the product genuinely improves consultant performance.
